questions.text: Unlike the Knights of Labor, which tried to organize nearly all workers, the American Federation of Labor, founded in 1886, organized workers by

answers.text: political party membership.
region of the country.
religious denomination.
skilled craft.

questions.feedback_general: Samuel Gompers's AFL deliberately narrowed its focus to organized craft workers and concrete workplace demands.

questions.text: During the 1894 Pullman boycott, Eugene Debs's American Railway Union refused to handle any train pulling a Pullman car, stopping rail traffic across much of the country. What was the outcome for Debs personally?

answers.text: He was elected to Congress as a reward for his leadership.
He was appointed U.S. Secretary of Labor.
He was imprisoned for defying a federal court order, and emerged from prison a socialist.
He retired from labor activism entirely once the boycott ended peacefully.

questions.feedback_general: His prison term is the direct link between the labor movement and the rise of American socialism this course traces into Week 11.

questions.text: Ida Tarbell's multi-part investigation of Standard Oil, published in McClure's Magazine beginning in 1902, relied on years of documented research rather than rumor or opinion. Why did this method matter to the investigation's ultimate impact on public opinion and, eventually, on Standard Oil's 1911 breakup?

answers.text: It did not matter; sensational, undocumented claims would have had the same persuasive effect.
Documented, verifiable research made Tarbell's charges much harder for Standard Oil to dismiss as mere gossip, giving the case for reform real evidentiary weight.
Tarbell's method made no difference because Standard Oil was already scheduled for dissolution before she began writing.
Her research was ignored entirely until the Sherman Antitrust Act was first passed, in 1890.

questions.feedback_general: Standard Oil could have brushed off rumor. Years of documents were much harder to answer.

questions.text: Jane Addams's Hull House and the broader Social Gospel movement responded to industrial-era urban poverty by

answers.text: offering education, childcare, and legal aid to immigrant neighbors while documenting conditions to support reform.
arguing that poverty was solely a matter of personal moral failure requiring no institutional response.
calling for the abolition of all private charity in favor of government-run workhouses.
relocating urban poor populations to rural farming communities by federal order.

questions.feedback_general: This is the settlement house model exactly as this course's Week 8 lesson presents it.

questions.text: In Plessy v. Ferguson (1896), the Supreme Court upheld racial segregation under the doctrine of "separate but equal," with Justice John Marshall Harlan alone dissenting and arguing the Constitution is "color blind." Considered together, what does the case's outcome and Harlan's lone dissent suggest about legal protections for Black Americans in this period?

answers.text: That the 14th Amendment's equal protection guarantee was fully and consistently enforced by the courts throughout the Gilded Age.
That Harlan's dissent immediately overturned segregation nationwide.
That segregation laws were struck down by every other Supreme Court case decided in the 1890s.
That formal constitutional guarantees existed on paper, but a near-unanimous Court majority allowed states to circumvent their practical effect for decades.

questions.feedback_general: The holding and the lone dissent have to be read together. A guarantee written into the Constitution did not, by itself, produce equal treatment.

questions.text: Under the crop lien system, a merchant advanced credit to a farmer against a future harvest at high interest. What was the typical long-term effect of this system on Southern sharecroppers, Black and white alike?

answers.text: It allowed most sharecroppers to buy their own land within a few years.
It was outlawed by the federal government almost immediately after Reconstruction ended.
It frequently trapped farmers in cycles of debt they could not escape from one harvest to the next.
It eliminated the need for sharecropping entirely by 1880.

questions.feedback_general: The crop lien tied a farmer's next harvest to a debt already owed, which is the same mechanism running through sharecropping and debt peonage.

questions.text: Newspapers owned by Joseph Pulitzer and William Randolph Hearst competed for readers in the late 1890s by publishing sensational, sometimes exaggerated stories about Spanish conduct in Cuba. This style of reporting became known as

answers.text: yellow journalism.
muckraking.
the Social Gospel.
preservationism.

questions.feedback_general: The term comes from the "Yellow Kid" comic character both papers ran during their circulation war, per this course's Week 9 lesson.

questions.text: The Teller Amendment, attached to the 1898 declaration of war, disclaimed any U.S. intention of annexing Cuba. How did the 1901 Platt Amendment relate to this earlier promise?

answers.text: It fully honored the Teller Amendment by granting Cuba complete independence with no restrictions.
It limited Cuba's independence by reserving an American right to intervene there, in tension with Teller's earlier promise.
It formally annexed Cuba as a U.S. territory, directly contradicting Teller.
It had no connection to Cuba at all and applied only to the Philippines.

questions.feedback_general: Teller promised no annexation. Platt reserved an American right to intervene. The two sit uneasily together, and that gap is the point.

questions.text: After the Treaty of Paris transferred the Philippines to the United States, Filipino independence leader Emilio Aguinaldo's forces fought American troops rather than accept new colonial rule, while the Anti-Imperialist League, including Mark Twain and Andrew Carnegie, opposed American control of the islands at home. Taken together, what tension in the case for American empire do these two facts illustrate?

answers.text: That every Filipino leader welcomed American rule as an improvement over Spanish rule.
That the Anti-Imperialist League supported the war against Aguinaldo's forces.
That Aguinaldo and the Anti-Imperialist League had no shared position of any kind.
That the same nation which had recently criticized European colonization also acquired an overseas empire, exposing a tension its own citizens and the Filipinos both noticed.

questions.feedback_general: A nation that had recently criticized European colonization acquired an overseas empire of its own. Filipinos fighting American troops and Americans opposing the war at home both noticed.

Front Matter

Course Syllabus · Fall 2026

Reproduced from the official course syllabus for facilitator reference

Facilitator: Dr. Rob Reed · rreed@optimaed.com · Canvas Inbox  |  Florida Course: 2100310, One Credit, Fall Semester  |  Grade Level: 10  |  Format: On-Demand, also offered live on Optima's VR campus  |  Office Hours: Tue & Thu, 9:15–11:59 AM and 2:00–3:00 PM

Course Overview

HS U.S. History: Reconstruction to Present is a 10th grade study of American history from Reconstruction through World War I. Scholars examine the political settlement after the Civil War, the Gilded Age's industrial transformation, the labor movement and urbanization, Progressive Era reforms, American imperial expansion, and U.S. entry into World War I, using primary sources (including Theodore Roosevelt's extensive writings) and virtual reality to engage with the key people and events of this era.

Important Dates · Fall 2026

  • Aug 12, 2026 · First day of school
  • Sep 7, 2026 · Labor Day, school closed
  • Sep 12, 2026 · Q1 Primary Source Reports milestone
  • Oct 9, 2026 · Quarter 1 ends
  • Oct 12, 2026 · Columbus Day, school closed
  • Nov 7, 2026 · Q2 Primary Source Reports milestone
  • Nov 11, 2026 · Veterans' Day, school closed
  • Nov 23–27, 2026 · Thanksgiving break
  • Dec 18, 2026 · Quarter 2 ends, fall semester ends

Assessment & Grading

  • 60% Asynchronous Homework: reading quizzes, primary source reports, VR activity write-ups
  • 30% Projects: extended primary source analyses and quarter capstone submissions
  • 10% Synchronous Homework & Activities: live class participation and discussion

Delivery, AI Use, and Being an Optima Scholar

The course is offered both On-Demand (self-paced within each quarter) and Live (synchronous, on Optima's VR campus); both share identical content and expectations. AI tools may support learning but may never substitute for a scholar's own thinking on graded work. Every scholar is expected to practice Optima's seven virtues (courage, courtesy, honesty, perseverance, self-government, service, and responsibility) and to engage the course's VR campus and Microsoft 365 tools as seriously as any physical classroom or notebook.
